Figure 6 The color-gadget for a color A ∈ C where A = {a1, a2, a3, a4} nodes. Each node ai corresponds to the gap between the vertex-pairs (a⊤i−1, a⊥i−1) and (a⊤i , a⊥i ). In order to reach all a⊥-vertices, we need to delay P→A (blue) and P←A (green) at adjacent vertex-pairs in order to switch onto them from Ps (black). Such delaying operations cost at least (|A| − 1) · ω.

Figure 11 Illustration of the guessed values for a non-root base-path Q with parent P . ℓQ is the difference between the labels of the temporal edges eP and eQ entering and leaving the switch vertex vQ. The active delay δQ is applied to eQ; the active advance αQ is derived as ←AQ − AQ ←. The values D→Q , ←AQ, AQ ← describe the delay/advance propagations on P at vQ, and ϕQ ← the advance arriving at vQ from Q’s children.

Table 1 Overview of our results. All settings are NP-hard. The rows show the parameterized complexity of the MaxReach problem variants with respect to the number of base-paths k, the budget b, and their combination; “fxd SPT” stands for “fixed switch-path-tree” which denotes the special case where the order in which we have to traverse the base-paths is additionally given. The b = ∞ column represents our results for delaying/advancing/shifting without a budget constraint, so there is no parameterization by b.
